architecture.mechanism: Battery-free wireless power harvesting via near-field communication (NFC) sustains device operation with an unlimited power supply instead of draining a stored battery.
architecture.intervention: Convert the F-150's key-off loads (door status sensing, infotainment keep-alive, back-over camera) to NFC/wirelessly-powered, wake-on-demand modules that draw quiescent current from a wireless field rather than the 12 V battery, with duty-cycling so they activate only on door handle, reverse-gear, or user events.
architecture.expected_effect: Parasitic battery drain during key-off falls to near zero while door status, infotainment, and back-over camera remain operational and safety-linked functions (lock state, reverse camera activation) are preserved.
architecture.falsification_test: Clamp a current shunt on the battery negative terminal and log key-off quiescent current over 48 h for stock vs. NFC-powered duty-cycled modules; the mechanism is falsified if drain does not drop below OEM parasitic spec (typically ~50 mA) or if camera/door-status/infotainment response latency exceeds specification.
